At its meeting on 21 January 2014, the Monetary Council reviewed the latest economic and financial developments and voted to reduce the central bank base rate by 15 basis points from 3.00% to 2.85%, with effect from 22 January 2014.
In the Council’s judgement, Hungarian economic growth is likely to continue this year and next.

At its meeting on 21 January 2014, the Monetary Council reviewed the latest economic and financial developments and voted to reduce the central bank base rate by 15 basis points from 3.00% to 2.85%, with effect from 22 January 2014.
In the Council’s judgement, Hungarian economic growth is likely to continue this year and next.
While the pace of activity is strengthening, the level of output remains below its potential and is likely to return close to that level at the end of the horizon relevant for monetary policy.
With employment rising steadily, the unemployment rate is falling, but still exceeds its long-term level determined by structural factors.
